item.title: What really happened between DJ Akademiks and SummyahMarie that led to legal action? Controversy explained
item.description: DJ Akademiks and streamer SummyahMarie are in an ongoing online dispute after he accused her of being part of “escort culture.” She denied the claims during a January 10, 2026 livestream and later shared text messages showing she sent him a cease-and-desist letter. Both continue to defend their positions publicly.

item.title: YouTube now lets creators earn full ad revenue on non-graphic content about controversial issues
item.description: YouTube has updated its monetization policy, now allowing creators to earn ad revenue from videos discussing sensitive topics like abortion and abuse. Previously, such content was often demonetized, even for educational purposes. The new guidelines permit monetization for non-graphic dramatizations or discussions, aiming to foster valuable conversations while reassuring advertisers.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: ‘Told on good authority’: Donald Trump says killing of protesters in Iran 'stopping’; claims 'no plans for executions'
item.description: President Donald Trump stated Iran's executions are halting. He received this information from a reliable source. Trump had previously assured protestors of US support. His administration is reviewing options, including diplomatic and military actions. Reports indicate thousands have been killed by Iranian security forces during recent protests.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Not blaming anybody': Renee Good's Republican father-in-law speaks out after fatal ICE shooting
item.description: A former father-in-law of Renee Nicole Good, a poet and mother killed by ICE, has broken his silence. Timmy Macklin, a Trump supporter, expressed sympathy but questioned Good's actions. He also criticized the ICE agent's language post-shooting, urging him to find faith. Macklin acknowledged Trump's remarks about Good's 'tough actions' while maintaining his own support for the President.

item.title: US Navy sailor Jinchao Wei betrays America by spying for China – inside the secret mission
item.description: In a significant breach of trust, ex-US Navy sailor Jinchao Wei has received a sentence exceeding 16 years behind bars. Wei engaged in espionage by selling critical military information, including intricate technical manuals and operational specifics on US Navy vessels, to a Chinese intelligence agent, pocketing over $12,000 in the process.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Watch: ICE agents smash window, drag 'disabled' woman from car in Minneapolis protest clash
item.description: Minneapolis faces protests after ICE agents arrest a disabled woman. Video shows agents smashing a car window and removing the woman. She stated she was going to a doctor. ICE officials warn against interference. The agency claims the woman obstructed an operation to arrest an Ecuadorian man. Six others were arrested for assaulting officers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Number one country to ban visas from...’: Nikki Haley calls for China-first restrictions after US freezes visas for 75 countries
item.description: Former US envoy Nikki Haley has urged America to make China its top priority for visa restrictions, highlighting immigration and national security concerns. This statement emerges as the US prepares to temporarily halt immigrant visa processing for citizens of 75 nations, including Russia and Iran, starting January 2026, citing enhanced 'public charge' rule scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Adin Ross faces backlash from Doechii controversy and may quit Kick temporarily
item.description: Streamer Adin Ross faces significant backlash and a reported 30% drop in Kick earnings after making offensive remarks about rapper Doechii and other Black women. Despite pledges to Black-owned businesses and denials of racism, the controversy has impacted his reputation and partnerships, leading to speculation about a temporary break from streaming.

item.title: 'Fundamental disagreement’: Denmark holds talks with White House officials over Greenland; Trump pushes US control of island
item.description: US President Trump's renewed calls for NATO to help acquire Greenland have met with a 'fundamental disagreement' from Danish and Greenlandic officials. Despite US pressure, Denmark announced plans to bolster its military presence in the Arctic, citing an unpredictable security environment. Greenlandic representatives questioned the US approach, highlighting low local support for annexation.

item.title: ICE killed woman: Agent Jonathan Ross who shot Minneapolis’ Renee Good hospitalised with internal bleeding
item.description: An ICE officer, Jonathan Ross, shot and killed Renee Good after she allegedly struck him with her SUV. Ross suffered internal bleeding following the incident. Good's death intensified tensions between Minnesota and the federal government, leading to protests and a state lawsuit to block federal immigration enforcement.

item.description: Recognizing Greenland's pivotal role in national defense, President Trump emphasizes its importance for the 'Golden Dome' missile defense initiative. item.title: US freezes visa processing for 75 countries: Is India, Pakistan in the list? Check the complete details
item.description: The US State Department has halted immigrant visa processing for 75 countries, including Somalia, Russia, and Pakistan, effective January 21. This indefinite pause is part of a reassessment of visa processing procedures. The department aims to crack down on applicants as part of this new initiative.

item.title: Middle East on boil: US asks military personnel to depart bases; Iran issues warning
item.description: United States forces are repositioning from key Middle East bases. Tensions with Iran are rising sharply. This follows a crackdown on protests and threats of US military action. Iran warns of attacks on US bases if America strikes. Some personnel are advised to leave Qatar's Al Udeid Air Base. This is described as a posture change amid regional instability.
